intended_object: The verum (⊤) formula of the basic modal language. Here ⊤ is not a primitive symbol; it is defined as the abbreviation ⊥ → ⊥. This is inferred from the name and from the parallel `verum` definition in the same file.
explanation: The modal formula type has only these primitives: atoms, ⊥, → and □. In that setting the standard definition of ⊤ is ⊥ → ⊥, and that is exactly what `top` is (`imp falsum falsum`). It is identical to the `verum` definition two lines above, so it is just an alias. It is defined for formulas over any type of atoms `α`, so it is fully general. Mathlib has no modal-logic syntax, so it has no counterpart.
